2026-12-21.title: Fourth Monday of Annunciation
2026-12-21.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: In the beginning was the Word
2026-12-21.verse: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
theo: Four days before Christmas the Church reads the opening of John's Gospel. Before Bethlehem there is eternity: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God… All things came into being through him… The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.” The child in the manger is the eternal Son, Creator of all.

Paul asks the Ephesians to “pray in the Spirit at all times” and to pray for him, “that when I speak, a message may be given to me to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel.” In these last days of waiting, prayer prepares the heart to receive the Word made flesh.
outline: Ask: who is the child we will adore at Christmas?
The baby of Bethlehem is God from all eternity.
No darkness can overcome his light.
Prayer opens the heart to the Word.
live: Read the Prologue slowly each day until Christmas.
Turn short moments of the day into prayer.
2026-12-21.prayer: Eternal Word of the Father, light of every person, shine in my darkness and prepare my heart to welcome you at Christmas. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the eternal Word, through whom all things were made, comes to us under the form of bread. The light that shone in Bethlehem shines on our altar.

quick: The child of Bethlehem is the eternal Word.
The darkness cannot overcome his light.
Prayer prepares the heart to receive him.
2026-12-21.action: Read John 1:1–14 each day until Christmas.
2026-12-21.question: Where is the darkness in my life that Christ must enlighten?

family.explain: Before the world was made, Jesus was with God. He is the light that darkness can never put out.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel they live in darkness this Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “Let us light a candle tonight. Where do we need Jesus' light?”

pm.open: Eternal Word of the Father, light of the world, shine on us as we gather. Teach us to pray at all times and give us boldness to proclaim you. Amen.
share: Paul asks for boldness to proclaim the Gospel (Ephesians 6:19). Where do I lack courage to speak of Christ?
The light shines in the darkness (John 1:5). What darkness in my life needs his light?
How will I pray more in these last days before Christmas?
pm.resp: Christ our light, shine upon us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mystery of the Word made flesh with boldness.
For persecuted Christians, that they may be strengthened by prayer.
For priests and preachers, that they may speak with courage this Christmas.
For those in darkness, illness or despair, that Christ's light may reach them.
For our families, that we may pray together in these holy days.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, eternal Word, you came as light into our darkness. Keep us alert in prayer and bold in witness, and let your light shine through us this Christmas. Amen.

illus: During a power cut in a Kottayam hostel, a student lit a single candle in the corridor. One by one, others came out with their own candles and lit them from it. Soon the corridor was full of light. One small light, shared, overcame the darkness.

homily: Dear friends, with four days to Christmas, St Paul asks us to pray: pray in the Spirit at all times in every prayer and supplication; keep alert and always persevere in supplication for all the saints. Pray also for me, so that I may make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel (Ephesians 6:18–19).
Paul wrote this from prison, in chains. Yet he does not ask for release; he asks for boldness to speak. Prayer gave him courage.

In the Gospel we hear the opening of St John: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things came into being through him. In him was life, and the life was the light of all people. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it (John 1:1–5).

This is the deepest meaning of Christmas. The baby in the manger is not merely a good person who later became holy. He is the eternal Word, through whom all things were made. The One who made the stars lies under the star of Bethlehem.

And the darkness did not overcome it. Whatever darkness you face this Christmas, sickness, loneliness, debt, grief, sin, the light of Christ is stronger. It may seem small, like one candle, but darkness cannot put it out.

These last days before Christmas, let us pray more: at home, in the church, before the crib. Let us pray for missionaries, for persecuted Christians, for our priests, that they may proclaim the Gospel with boldness. And let us light a candle in our home each evening, saying: the light shines in the darkness. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the light of the world. When you light the star or lamp this Christmas, remember that Jesus is the true Light!

intro: Theme: “The light shines in the darkness.”
The Prologue of John: the eternal Word who comes as a child.

sub: The Word is God from eternity.
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.
In him was life, and the life was the light of all people. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
points.apply: Bring one dark situation into Christ's light in prayer.

sub: The Son is begotten, not made.
At Christmas he is born in time.
q: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being.
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly, pausing at “begotten, not made”.

concl: The Word through whom all was made is coming as a child.
Let his light shine in us.
2026-12-21.resolve: Read the Prologue each day until Christmas.
